newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila has enough rice stocks to weather El Nino.
newsitem.headline: Manila has enough rice stocks to weather El Nino.

text.p: The Philippines' state-owned National Food Authority on Tuesday sought to allay fears of a looming food shortage at the onset of a dry spell brought by the El Nino phenomenon, saying the country had enough rice stocks.

NFA administrator Joemarie Gerochi made the announcement after one of the country's leading agricultural experts predicted the country would have to import 950,000 tonnes of rice early next year to mitigate the impact of the dry spell.
"There is no cause for alarm as the inventory of the government rice through the NFA and that of the whole industry is sufficient to bridge us to the next harvest," Gerochi said in a statement.

But Rolando Dy, director for the Institute of Agribusiness Development and Policy of the University of Asia and the Pacific, said the country has to start booking import orders for rice to be delivered early next year.
"For the rest of 1997, we are adequately secured. But for the first half of 1998, we have to make advance orders," Dy said in a telephone interview.
Dy said he expected the Philippine rice harvest to drop to 2.7 million tonnes in the first half of 1998 compared with 3.2 million in same period this year.
Gerochi said the Philippines has 2.022 million tonnes of rice stocks, of which 734,300 tonnes are stored in NFA warehouses.
"Based on the average daily rice requirement of 22,000 tonnes, the current stocks is sufficient to last for more than three months," he said.
"The recommendation of Dy to import up to 950,000 tonnes of rice allegedly to ensure adequate supply of the staple until next year is a projected worst scenario on the effects of El Nino." he added.
The Agriculture Department said it had dug wells and started cloud seeding in areas where the volume of rainfall was low.
Philippine rice crop is seasonally lean in the third quarter.
Nevertheless, Gerochi said should importation become necessary becaue of the El Nino it will be done at the proper time and at a volume that is not disruptive to local farmers.
